brief.headline: Claude Code 2.1.222 closes a worktree escape hooks couldn't block
brief.summary:
Update tonight, before anything else: Claude Code 2.1.222 fixes isolated worktree subagents being able to run destructive git commands against your main checkout, and stops PreToolUse auto-allow hooks from getting bypassed on background tasks — this is a hole in exactly the worktree-plus-hooks setup you run unattended. claude-code-router also shipped v3.0.19 with a Codex-provider fix and a timing-attack patch on gateway API-key comparison, worth pulling if you proxy through it.

On top of the patch, there's a real stack forming for trustworthy unattended PRs: fablize and fable-method both distill a think/act/prove verification loop that forces evidence before Opus calls something done, ponytail biases agents toward smaller diffs so the morning review is faster, and codeseek gives agents call-graph/semantic search context before they edit. For cost, LFM2.5-2.6B now runs tool-calling at 30 tok/s in under 2.5GB RAM — a real candidate for offloading cheap subagent glue work off your main API bill — and Homebench plus token-monitor let you measure and track that shift on your own hardware instead of guessing. If you want off-desk control, devspace turns a phone browser tab into a Claude Code or Codex session with no terminal required.
bullets: Update Claude Code to 2.1.222 — fixes worktree subagents reaching the main checkout and PreToolUse hook bypass on background tasks
Update claude-code-router to v3.0.19 — fixes a Codex-provider 404 and a timing-attack gateway API-key check
Try fablize or fable-method's think/act/prove eval to force evidence and verification before Opus ships a PR
Drop ponytail's skill in to bias agents toward smaller diffs and faster morning review
Run LFM2.5-2.6B (Q4_K_M GGUF, under 2.5GB RAM) in llama.cpp for cheap tool-calling subagent steps
Benchmark local models with Homebench and track per-tool spend with token-monitor before moving subagents off paid APIs

signals.label: Self-verification before shipping a PR
signals.note: fablize, fable-method, and ponytail all target the same problem: fewer wrong or bloated overnight diffs landing unreviewed.

signals.label: Cheap/local models for subagent glue work
signals.note: LFM2.5-2.6B on-phone, Homebench, token-monitor, and dao-code's DeepSeek-V4 cache routing all point at moving trivial subagent steps off paid hosted calls.

signals.label: Multi-harness and multi-provider control planes
signals.note: opencodex, claudexor, and omnigent are all converging on one control layer that swaps models/harnesses under Claude Code without a rewrite.

signals.label: Away-from-desk agent control
signals.note: devspace and omnigent give phone/browser control, but it's still early tooling rather than a settled pattern.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.222 fixes worktree-isolated sessions (and their subagents) being able to run destructive git commands against the main checkout, and stops PreToolUse auto-allow hooks from bypassing tool restrictions in background agent tasks.
items.whyItMatters: This is a real hole in exactly the worktree-plus-hooks setup he runs unattended — an isolated subagent could previously reach the main checkout with destructive commands.
items.tryThis: Update Claude Code to 2.1.222 now if you run worktree-isolated sessions or rely on PreToolUse auto-allow hooks.

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: 'Ponytail' is a prompt/skill package that makes your AI coding agent behave like a lazy senior dev, aggressively avoiding unnecessary code.
items.whyItMatters: Directly shrinks the diffs an agent produces overnight, making the resulting PR faster to review at your desk in the morning.
items.tryThis: Drop ponytail's prompt/skill into your agent config to bias it toward writing less code before opening a PR.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering is a repo of CLI patterns for orchestrating AI coding agents, including loop-audit, loop-init, and loop-cost commands.
items.whyItMatters: These are concrete CLI tools for auditing agent loops and tracking their cost — exactly the unattended-run tooling and cost visibility you're after.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering, run `loop-init` on your current agent setup, then `loop-cost` to see per-run spend.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: The 'fablize' Claude Code plugin enforces completion, evidence, and verification as procedure so Opus only ships changes proven transferable in an internal comparison.
items.whyItMatters: This is exactly the kind of self-verification harness that lets you leave an agent running unattended and trust the resulting PR more.
items.tryThis: Install the fablize plugin in Claude Code to add enforced evidence/verification steps before Opus finishes a task.

items.title: v3.0.19
items.tldr: claude-code-router 3.0.19 fixes a Codex-provider 404, adds routed-model visibility in request logs, syncs local Codex OAuth credentials, and switches gateway API-key comparison to constant-time.
items.whyItMatters: Patches both a real routing bug and a timing-attack gateway vulnerability if he's routing Claude Code traffic through this proxy to mix providers.
items.tryThis: Update claude-code-router to v3.0.19, especially if you route through a Codex provider or expose the gateway with an API key.

items.title: A 2.6B model with tool calling and 128K context now runs at 30 tok/s on a phone
items.tldr: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-2.6B is a 2.69B tool-calling model with 128K context that runs at 30 tok/s on a phone and under 2.5GB RAM as a 1.67GB Q4_K_M GGUF, already working in llama.cpp.
items.whyItMatters: Small and fast enough to run locally for cheap subagent steps (routing, tool-call glue, formatting) instead of burning hosted API calls on trivial work.
items.tryThis: Pull the Q4_K_M GGUF and load it in llama.cpp to route cheap tool-calling subagent steps off your main model.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and custom agents under one policy/sandboxing layer, swappable without rewriting, controllable from any device.
items.whyItMatters: Gives a single control plane to sandbox whatever agent is running and to check on or steer overnight jobs remotely instead of being tied to a terminal.
items.tryThis: Clone omnigent-ai/omnigent and wire your Claude Code worktree setup through it to test its sandbox policies and remote-device control.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is an open-source proxy that lets Codex CLI/App/SDK and Claude Code call any backend model — Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, local Ollama — instead of the vendor default.
items.whyItMatters: Lets him route cheap or local models into his existing Claude Code setup for background/verification subagents without switching harnesses.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point a background/verification subagent at a local Ollama model instead of your primary provider.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace turns the ChatGPT web app into a Codex-style coding agent, or Claude's web chat into a Claude Code session.
items.whyItMatters: A way to kick off or steer coding-agent work from a phone/browser chat interface without a terminal, matching the away-from-desk control he's after.
items.tryThis: Install Waishnav/devspace and drive one coding task from the ChatGPT or Claude web app on your phone instead of a terminal.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills a 'think / act / prove' workflow into portable skills with a built-in eval, meant to make any model check its own work before finishing.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete self-verification pattern he can drop into his own subagent pipeline to cut down on unreviewed, wrong overnight output.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and adapt its think/act/prove skill plus eval as a pre-PR verification step in your own agent pipeline.

items.title: tigicion/dao-code — Open-source TypeScript terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 — builds on DeepSeek's strong price-performance and ultra-cheap cache pricing, engineering byte-stable prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory
items.tldr: dao-code is a terminal coding agent built for DeepSeek-V4 that uses byte-stable prompt prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory costs almost nothing under DeepSeek's cache pricing.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete path to moving long-running background subagents onto a much cheaper model+cache combo instead of paying full price for idle loops, and it's Claude Code config compatible.
items.tryThis: Clone tigicion/dao-code, point it at DeepSeek-V4, and route an overnight background job through it to compare cache cost against your current model.

items.title: Javis603/token-monitor — Local-first desktop widget for tracking token usage, costs, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and OpenClaw—with multi-device sync.
items.tldr: token-monitor is a local-first desktop widget tracking token usage, cost and limits across 28+ AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw) with multi-device sync.
items.whyItMatters: Gives concrete per-tool spend visibility so he can decide which subagents to move to cheaper models instead of guessing.
items.tryThis: Install Javis603/token-monitor and check it after a night of unattended runs to see which harness or model burned the budget.

items.title: withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit — Your AI forgets. This remembers. Spec-driven coding harness for vibecoders, product owners, CEOs and real builders — self-improving context memory, 15 agents, 33 skills working with /goal, agent-team, & work
items.tldr: vibecode-pro-max-kit is a spec-driven Claude Code/Codex harness with persistent context memory and 15 agents/33 skills built to run 'autopilot loops' with zero human gate.
items.whyItMatters: Directly targets the describe-it-and-sleep workflow he's after — worth a real overnight test to see if the autopilot loop actually holds up unattended.
items.tryThis: Clone withkynam/vibecode-pro-max-kit and run its /goal + agent-team autopilot loop on one real ticket overnight.

items.title: CodeBendKit/codeseek — Rust-powered code intelligence CLI for AI coding agents. Builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (Dense + Sparse + RRF + Reranker) across 7 languages. Ships as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: codeseek is a Rust CLI that builds call graphs and hybrid dense+sparse+reranker semantic search indexes across 7 languages, shipped as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Sharper call-graph/semantic context before an agent edits code is a direct lever on unattended-run reliability and reviewable-PR quality.
items.tryThis: Clone CodeBendKit/codeseek, index your mobile app repo, and register it as an MCP server in Claude Code's config.

items.title: razzant/claudexor — Multi-harness control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode: quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shared thread context, and cross-model review.
items.tldr: claudexor is a control plane that quota-rotates across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shares thread context, and runs cross-model review across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode.
items.whyItMatters: Quota-aware rotation directly cuts cost and avoids rate-limit stalls on unattended overnight runs, and cross-model review is a free second opinion before a PR lands.
items.tryThis: Clone razzant/claudexor, add your extra Claude/Codex subscriptions, and let it auto-rotate quota for long unattended runs.

items.title: Homebench – Benchmark local LLMs for speed, memory, and quality
items.tldr: 'Homebench' is a benchmark tool for measuring local LLM speed, memory, and quality on your own machine.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a concrete way to decide which local model to route cheap subagent work to, based on your actual hardware rather than leaderboard numbers.
items.tryThis: Run Homebench on your machine to pick which local model gets the cheap/background subagent work.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.222
items.tldr: Claude Code v2.1.222 ships with 3 improvements and 16 fixes.
items.whyItMatters: You run Claude Code as your primary overnight harness, so a fix-heavy release is worth pulling before your next unattended run.
items.tryThis: Update to Claude Code v2.1.222 before your next overnight agent run to pick up the 16 fixes.

items.title: llm-anthropic 0.26
items.tldr: llm-anthropic 0.26 adds claude-fable-5/sonnet-5/opus-5 model IDs and moves web search, fetch, and code execution to the LLM CLI's -T tool interface, replacing the old -o web_search flags.
items.whyItMatters: If you script Claude through Simon Willison's llm CLI, old -o web_search flags now break until you switch to -T; new model IDs need to land in any hardcoded configs.
items.tryThis: Run `llm install -U llm-anthropic llm` and replace any `-o web_search*` usage with `-T WebSearch`/`-T WebFetch`/`-T CodeExecution`.

items.title: New release of LLM adds support for reasoning traces, OpenAI Responses, server-side tools, and smarter logging
items.tldr: LLM 0.32 adds visible reasoning traces (printed to stderr), OpenAI Responses API support, server-side provider tools, and redesigned content-addressable SQLite logging.
items.whyItMatters: If you pipe llm CLI output into scripts or other agents, reasoning traces now leak to stderr by default and could pollute automated pipelines.
items.tryThis: Run `pip install -U llm` and add `-R`/`--hide-reasoning` in any scripted/unattended llm CLI calls to keep stderr clean.

items.title: Show HN: Maple-Preview – Ternary 20B MoE running at 120 tok/s on a iPhone
items.tldr: Show HN demo 'Maple-Preview' runs a ternary 20B MoE model at 120 tok/s on an iPhone.
items.whyItMatters: On-device inference at that speed on consumer mobile hardware is directly relevant if you're weighing an in-app local model for your own mobile products.
items.tryThis: Pull the Maple-Preview demo/repo from the Show HN post and benchmark ternary-MoE inference speed on your own iPhone hardware.

items.title: KunAgent/Kun — Local-first AI agent workspace for coding, writing, design, research, and automation — one runtime for desktop GUI and TUI.
items.tldr: 'Kun' is a local-first AI agent workspace covering coding, writing, design, research and automation in one desktop GUI/TUI runtime.
items.whyItMatters: A local-first runtime is a candidate for routing background subagent work off paid cloud APIs.
items.tryThis: Try Kun as a local-first runtime for offloading background subagent tasks from cloud APIs.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: AutoCVE is an agent-driven platform that automates CVE discovery, vulnerability verification, and report generation on source code.
items.whyItMatters: It's a candidate subagent or hook for auditing a PR's security before your morning review, adding automated verification to an unattended pipeline.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and point it at a branch to see if it flags anything before your morning PR review.

items.title: ongridio/ongrid — An ops AI Agent that understands your infrastructure, finds the root cause, and fixes it — right from Slack, Telegram, Lark or DingTalk.
items.tldr: 'Ongrid' is an ops AI agent that diagnoses and fixes infrastructure issues, triggered from Slack, Telegram, Lark, or DingTalk.
items.whyItMatters: It's a working example of a chat-bridge pattern for triggering and monitoring agents away from your desk, even though it's built for ops rather than coding.
items.tryThis: Look at ongrid's Slack/Telegram trigger wiring as a template for controlling your own coding agents remotely.

items.title: yan5xu/codexloom — Turn Codex threads into an organization of long-lived domain agents.
items.tldr: codexloom turns OpenAI Codex CLI threads into persistent, long-lived domain agents instead of one-off sessions.
items.whyItMatters: It's a pattern for keeping agent context and identity alive across runs, useful for organizing subagents that keep working while you're away from the desk.
items.tryThis: Clone yan5xu/codexloom and wrap one long-running Codex thread as a persistent domain agent to test it.

clusters.title: Claude Code 2.1.222 patches worktree isolation and hook bypass
clusters.summary: Same release reported by two sources: fixes destructive git commands leaking from isolated worktree subagents into the main checkout, plus a PreToolUse auto-allow hook bypass on background tasks.

clusters.title: Fable's think/act/prove verification distilled into portable skills
clusters.summary: Two independent projects package the same 'Fable' evidence-and-verification workflow as a Claude Code skill/plugin so any model checks its own work before finishing.

clusters.title: Simon Willison's llm CLI ships two updates
clusters.summary: llm-anthropic 0.26 adds new model IDs and moves web search/fetch/code execution to the -T tool interface; LLM 0.32 adds reasoning traces, OpenAI Responses support, and new logging — both change scripted/unattended llm CLI behavior.

clusters.title: Coding-capable models now run fast on phones
clusters.summary: LFM2.5-2.6B does tool-calling at 30 tok/s under 2.5GB RAM on a phone, and Maple-Preview runs a ternary 20B MoE at 120 tok/s on an iPhone — both usable for on-device or cheap-tier inference.

clusters.title: New control planes for mixing harnesses and model providers
clusters.summary: opencodex, claudexor, and omnigent each add a layer that lets Claude Code/Codex/Cursor sessions swap in other models or harnesses, rotate quota, or run cross-model review without switching your primary tool.
